children.text: oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devāḥ bhadraṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O <s>Devas</s> (gods); may we see what is auspicious
with our eyes, O [you who are] worthy of worship.
May we, praising [you] with firm limbs and bodies, enjoy the life-span allotted by the gods.

children.text: svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ |
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> of great fame grant us well-being; may <s>Pūṣan</s>, the all-knowing, grant us well-being.

children.text: svasti nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatir dadhātu ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Tārkṣya</s> (Garuḍa), of unimpeded course, grant us well-being; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> grant us well-being.
<s>Oṃ</s>. That [<s>Brahman</s>] is full (<s>pūrṇa</s>); this [universe] is full. From the full, the full arises.
When the full is taken from the full, the full alone remains.
<s>Oṃ</s> — this syllable (<s>akṣara</s>) is all this. Its explanation [is as follows]: the past,
the present, and the future — all this is indeed <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone.
And whatever else transcends the three times — that too is <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone.

body.text:
Verse 2
sarvaṃ hyetad brahmāyamātmā brahma so 'yamātmā catuṣpāt ||
body.translated_text:
Verse 2
All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. This <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is <s>Brahman</s>. This very <s>Ātman</s> has four quarters (<s>pādas</s>).

children.translated_text: Verse 3
The first quarter (<s>pāda</s>) is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, whose domain is the waking state, whose cognition is directed outward, who has seven limbs
and nineteen mouths, and who experiences the gross — [this is] the first quarter.
Verse 4
<s>Taijasa</s>, whose domain is the dream state, whose cognition is directed inward, who has seven limbs and nineteen mouths,
and who experiences the subtle — [this is] the second quarter.

children.text: yatra supto na kañcana kāmaṃ kāmayate na
children.translated_text: Where the sleeper desires no desire whatsoever, and
sees no dream — that is deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>).
<s>Prājña</s>, whose domain is deep sleep, who has become unified, who is a mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>) itself, who is full of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>),
who experiences bliss, whose mouth [i.e., instrument] is thought (<s>cetas</s>) — [this is] the third quarter.

body.text:
Verse 6
eṣa sarveśvara eṣa sarvajña eṣo 'ntaryāmyeṣa
yoniḥ sarvasya prabhavāpyayau hi bhūtānām
body.translated_text:
Verse 6
This is the lord of all (<s>sarveśvara</s>); this is the knower of all (<s>sarvajña</s>); this is the inner controller (<s>antaryāmī</s>); this is the source (<s>yoni</s>) of all — indeed, [this is] the origin and dissolution of all beings.

children.text: bahiḥ prajño vibhurviśvo hyantaḥ prajñastu taijasaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Viśva</s> [is] the cognizer of the external, the all-pervading; <s>Taijasa</s> [is] the cognizer of the internal.

children.text: ghanaprajñastathā prājña eka eva tridhā smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> [is] the cognizer of the dense [mass of consciousness]. The one alone is remembered as threefold.
Verse 2
<s>Viśva</s> [is situated] at the right eye; <s>Taijasa</s> [is] within the mind.

children.text: ākāśe ca hydi prājñastridhā dehe vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> [is] in the space within the heart. Thus [the Self] is established in three ways within the body.
Verse 3
<s>Viśva</s> always experiences the gross; <s>Taijasa</s> experiences the subtle.
<s>Prājña</s> likewise experiences bliss. Know the enjoyment to be threefold.
Verse 4

children.text: sthūlaṃ tarpayate viśvaṃ praviviktaṃ tu taijasam |
children.translated_text: The gross satisfies <s>Viśva</s>; the subtle [satisfies] <s>Taijasa</s>.

children.text: ānandaśca tathā prājñaṃ tridhā tṛptiṃ nibodhata ||
children.translated_text: Bliss likewise [satisfies] <s>Prājña</s>. Know the satisfaction to be threefold.
Verse 5

children.text: triṣu dhāmasu yadbhojyaṃ bhoktā yaśca prakīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: That which is to be enjoyed in the three states, and the enjoyer who is proclaimed —

children.text: vedaitadubhayaṃ yastu sa bhuñjāno na lipyate ||
children.translated_text: he who knows both these, though enjoying, is not tainted.
Verse 6
It is ascertained that [<s>Brahman</s>] is the origin of all existing things.
<s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath) brings forth all; [the supreme] <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) projects the individual conscious rays (<s>cetaḥ</s>) separately.
Verse 7
Some thinkers of creation regard [it] as a manifestation, a bringing forth.
By others, creation is imagined to be of the nature of dream and illusion (<s>māyā</s>).
Verse 8
Those who hold firm views on creation [say] that creation is the mere will of the Lord.
Those who contemplate time believe that beings are produced from time.
Verse 9
Some [say] creation is for the purpose of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>); others [say] it is for play (<s>krīḍā</s>).
[But] this is the very nature (<s>svābhāva</s>) of the Divine One — what desire could there be for one whose desires are [already] fulfilled?

body.text:
Verse 7
nāntaḥ prajñaṃ na bahiḥ prajñaṃ nobhayataḥ prajñaṃ
na prajñānaghanaṃ na prajñaṃ nāprajñam |

children.translated_text: [It is] invisible, beyond empirical dealing, ungraspable, without characteristics, unthinkable, beyond designation,
whose essence is the experience of the one Self (<s>ekātmapratyayasāra</s>), [in whom] the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) has ceased, peaceful,

children.text: śivamadvaitaṃ caturthaṃ manyante sa ātmā sa vijñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: auspicious (<s>śiva</s>), non-dual (<s>advaita</s>) — [this] they consider the fourth (<s>caturtha</s>). That is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self); that is to be known.

body.translated_text:
Verse 7
[<s>Turīya</s>] is not that which cognizes the internal, nor that which cognizes the external, nor that which cognizes both, nor a mass of cognition (<s>prajñānaghana</s>), nor cognizing, nor non-cognizing.

children.translated_text: Verse 10
[He is] the Lord (<s>Īśāna</s>) who brings about the cessation of all suffering, the imperishable master.
Non-dual among all entities, the resplendent one (<s>deva</s>), the fourth (<s>turya</s>), [is] remembered as all-pervading.
Verse 11
<s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> are considered to be bound by cause and effect.

children.text: prājñaḥ kāraṇabaddhastu dvau tau turye na siddhytaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> is bound by cause alone; but those two [bondages] are not established in <s>Turīya</s>.
Verse 12

children.text: nātmānaṃ na paraṃ caiva na satyaṃ nāpi cānṛtam |
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> cognizes neither the self nor another, neither truth nor falsehood —
nothing whatsoever. <s>Turīya</s> is the ever-seeing of all.
Verse 13
The non-apprehension of duality is common to both <s>Prājña</s> and <s>Turīya</s>.

children.text: bījanidrāyutaḥ prājñaḥ sā ca turye na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> is associated with the sleep of causal [ignorance] (<s>bījanidrā</s>); that [causal sleep] does not exist in <s>Turīya</s>.
Verse 14
The first two [<s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s>] are associated with dream and sleep; <s>Prājña</s> [is associated] with dreamless sleep.

children.text: na nidrāṃ naiva ca svapnaṃ turye paśyanti niścitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The knowers of truth see neither sleep nor dream in <s>Turīya</s>.
Verse 15
Dream [belongs to one] who apprehends things otherwise [than they are]; sleep [belongs to one] who does not know the reality.
When the error in both of these is dissolved, one attains the state of <s>Turīya</s> (the Fourth).
Verse 16
When the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), sleeping due to beginningless <s>māyā</s> (illusion), awakens,
then it realizes the unborn, sleepless, dreamless, non-dual reality.
Verse 17

children.text: prapañco yadi vidyeta nivarteta na saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: If the phenomenal world truly existed, it would certainly cease to exist, without doubt;
this duality is merely <s>māyā</s> (illusion); ultimately, there is only non-duality (<s>advaita</s>).
Verse 18
The imagined diversity would cease if it were imagined by anyone;

children.text: upadeśādayaṃ vādo jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: this teaching is for the sake of instruction; when the truth is known, duality does not exist.
Verse 8
This same <s>Ātman</s> (Self), with regard to the syllable, is <s>Oṃkāra</s>, considered letter by letter;

children.text: pādā mātrā mātrāśca pādā akāra ukāro makāra iti ||
children.translated_text: the quarters are the letters and the letters are the quarters: <s>a-kāra</s>, <s>u-kāra</s>, <s>ma-kāra</s>.
<s>Vaiśvānara</s>, whose sphere is the waking state, is <s>a-kāra</s>, the first
letter, because of pervasiveness (<s>āpti</s>) or because of being the first (<s>ādimat</s>). One who knows thus indeed attains all
desires and becomes the first.
<s>Taijasa</s>, whose sphere is the dream state, is <s>u-kāra</s>, the second letter, because of excellence (<s>utkarṣa</s>)
or because of being intermediate (<s>ubhayatva</s>). One who knows thus indeed raises the flow of knowledge and becomes equal to all;

children.text: bhavati nāsyābrahmavitkule bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: no one ignorant of <s>Brahman</s> is born in his family, one who knows thus.
Verse 11
<s>Prājña</s>, whose sphere is deep sleep, is <s>ma-kāra</s>, the third letter, because of measuring (<s>miti</s>) or because of absorption (<s>apīti</s>);

children.text: minoti ha vā idaṃ sarvamapītiśca bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: one who knows thus indeed measures all this and becomes one in whom all merge.
Verse 19
When one wishes to identify <s>Viśva</s> with <s>a-kāra</s>, the commonality of being first is prominent;
when one understands the letter correspondence, the commonality of pervasiveness is also apparent.
Verse 20
In identifying <s>Taijasa</s> with <s>u-kāra</s>, the commonality of excellence is clearly seen;
when one understands the letter correspondence, the commonality of being intermediate is likewise apparent.
Verse 21
In identifying <s>Prājña</s> with <s>ma-kāra</s>, the commonality of measuring is prominent;
when one understands the letter correspondence, the commonality of absorption is also apparent.
Verse 22

children.text: triṣu dhāmasu yastulyaṃ sāmānyaṃ vetti niścitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who knows with certainty the commonality equally in the three states,
that great sage is worthy of worship by all beings and is to be honored.
Verse 23
<s>A-kāra</s> leads to <s>Viśva</s>, <s>u-kāra</s> also to <s>Taijasa</s>,

children.text: makāraśca punaḥ prājñaṃ nāmātre vidyate gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>ma-kāra</s> again to <s>Prājña</s>; in the measureless (<s>amātra</s>), there is no destination.
The fourth (<s>turīya</s>) is without measure (<s>amātra</s>), beyond empirical dealings, the cessation of the phenomenal world, auspicious (<s>śiva</s>), non-dual (<s>advaita</s>);

children.text: evamoṅkāra ātmaiva saṃviśatyātmanātmānaṃ ya evaṃ veda |
children.translated_text: thus <s>Oṃkāra</s> is indeed the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). One who knows thus enters the Self by the Self.
One who knows thus.
Verse 24

children.text: oṅkāraṃ pādaśo vidyātpādā mātrā na saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should know <s>Oṃkāra</s> quarter by quarter; the quarters are the letters, without doubt.

children.text: oṅkāraṃ pādaśo jñātvā na kiñcidapi cintayet ||
children.translated_text: Having known <s>Oṃkāra</s> quarter by quarter, one should not think of anything else.
Verse 25

children.text: yuñjīta praṇave cetaḥ praṇavo brahma nirbhayam |
children.translated_text: One should fix the mind on <s>Praṇava</s>; <s>Praṇava</s> is the fearless <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: praṇave nityayuktasya na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: For one who is ever united with <s>Praṇava</s>, there is no fear anywhere.
Verse 26

children.text: praṇavo hyaparaṃ brahma praṇavaśca paraḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> is indeed the lower <s>Brahman</s>, and <s>Praṇava</s> is also considered the higher.
Without prior, without interior, without exterior, without successor — <s>Praṇava</s> is imperishable.
Verse 27
<s>Praṇava</s> is indeed the beginning, middle, and end of everything.

children.text: evaṃ hi praṇavaṃ jñātvā vyaśnute tadanantaram ||
children.translated_text: Having known <s>Praṇava</s> thus, one attains [<s>Brahman</s>] immediately thereafter.
Verse 28
One should know <s>Praṇava</s> as the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) seated in the heart of all.
Having contemplated the all-pervading <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the wise one does not grieve.
Verse 29
Without measure, of infinite measure, the auspicious cessation of duality —

children.text: oṅkāro vidito yena sa munirnetaro janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one by whom <s>Oṃkāra</s> is known, he is a sage, and no other person.
